title: De-duplication and Header Stripping Statistics
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'De-duplication and Header Stripping Statistics' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_de_duplication_and_header_stripping_statistics` (UC-5.17.6), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — De-duplication and Header Stripping Statistics", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=visibility` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `_time` satisfies `dedup_baseline` > 1 for UC-5.17.6 ('De-duplication and Header Stripping Statistics'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `visibility` / `target_sourcetype` events where `_time` stays below `dedup_baseline` > 1, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-5.17.6.

dataSources: Detailed: `index=visibility`; feature telemetry such as `gigamon:gigasmart`, `keysight:advanced_features`, `cpacket:analytics` exposing `dedup_removed_pct`, `strip_vlan_count`, `inner_ip_exposed`, `timestamp_normalized_events`, `payload_collapsed_frames`. Pair with tool-ingest byte counters (IDS/NDR) to sanity-check that stripping did not overshoot legitimate encapsulations. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Gigamon GigaSMART application intelligence integrations, Keysight Vision advanced processing modules, generic syslog parsers plus Splunk-field extractions for JSON feature counters. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=visibility earliest=-24h
| eval v=lower(sourcetype)
| eval vendor=case(match(v,"gigamon"),"Gigamon",match(v,"keysight|ixia|vision"),"Keysight",match(v,"cpacket|cstor"),"cPacket","other")
| where vendor!="other"
| eval feat_host=coalesce(host,chassis_name,"unknown")
| eval dedup_pct=tonumber(coalesce(dedup_removed_pct,payload_dedup_ratio*100,null()))
| eval strip_events=tonumber(coalesce(vlan_strip_count,header_strip_events,stripped_frames))
| bin _time span=1h
| stats avg(dedup_pct) as avg_dedup max(dedup_pct) as peak_dedup sum(strip_events) as strips by _time vendor feat_host feature_profile
| streamstats global=f window=24 avg(avg_dedup) as dedup_baseline by vendor feat_host feature_profile
| eval dedup_anomaly=if(peak_dedup>(dedup_baseline*3) AND dedup_baseline>1,1,0)
| eval strip_spike=if(strips>1000000,1,0)
| where dedup_anomaly=1 OR strip_spike=1
| sort - peak_dedup vendor feat_host _time
description: Hourly Splunk summarizes advanced-feature throughput shaping—duplicate removal ratios and header-strip volumes—so mis-tuned profiles that erase forensic VLAN tags or deduplicate away rare flows stop hiding inside opaque appliance dashboards.
value: Hourly Splunk summarizes advanced-feature throughput shaping—duplicate removal ratios and header-strip volu.... Timely UC-5.17.6 alerting on 'De-duplication and Header Stripping Statistics' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Document acceptable dedup ceilings per deployment tier; join Splunk results weekly with PCAP spot-checks on mirrored spans to validate retained headers match policy.
visualization: Stacked area chart of strips vs `_time`; overlaid line for avg_dedup; annotations from change-management lookup when profile hashes shift.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `visibility`** — Planned work for 'De-duplication and Header Stripping Statistics' shifts `avg` over `span=1h` while `_time` remains in-scope for UC-5.17.6. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `avg` on `configured_sourcetype`** — Scheduled automation elevates `vendor` without crossing `dedup_baseline` > 1. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `_time`** — Health checks in `visibility` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `configured_sourcetype`** — First 48h baseline for `_time` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `_time`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Signed architecture standards stating which encapsulations must survive to tools.
• Lab PCAP corpus replay harness feeding identical traffic through profiles under test.
• Namespaced `feature_profile` identifiers matching Git-managed templates.

Step 1 — Enable telemetry
Activate vendor counters for dedup sessions and strip engines; ensure logs include profile revision hashes after each deployment pipeline run.

Step 2 — Normalize percentages
Convert ratios to 0–100 scale consistently; ignore samples where denominator counters reset mid-hour.

Step 3 — Build Splunk content
Materialize summary index `visibility_feat_hourly` from the rolling stats for twelve-month trending without re-scanning raw noisy streams.

Step 4 — Validate
Replay PCAP through staging appliance toggling dedup on/off—ensure Splunk deltas align with wireshark difference summaries within agreed tolerance.

Step 5 — Operationalize
Alert only after sustained anomalies (three consecutive hours) to ignore transient microbursts; dashboard annotate recent change tickets pulled via REST lookup.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Gigamon GigaSMART application intelligence integrations, Keysight Vision advanced processing modules, generic syslog parsers plus Splunk-field extractions for JSON feature counters. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into visibility. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, dedup_anomaly, dedup_baseline, feat_host`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Before copies reach our watchers, machines sometimes remove repeats or peel off labels so the picture is clearer—but peel too much and we lose the story. We watch those knobs so trimming stays helpful instead of accidentally hiding clues.
